newsitem.title: UK: Euro Products Outlook - Firmer with crude supporti.
newsitem.headline: Euro Products Outlook - Firmer with crude supporti.

text.p: Most European oil products seem set for a more bullish week with crude's recent gains and better fundamentals across much of the barrel, traders said.

Gasoline prices are likely to firm a little with the NYMEX creeping higher offering the chance of arbitrage and pockets of buying beginning to appear in NWE after a recent lull that has caused stocks to build up in ARA.
"Some people are expecting gasoline to make a move higher and this has created some pockets of buying interest," one trader said.
"There hasn't been much buying from Germany recently so they may come in again soon but there's plenty of oil around," he added.
Light buying from Germany was seen on Friday but stocks in independent storage in ARA at 400-425,000 tonnes are still around 75,000 tonnes over levels this time last year, industry sources said.
Traders said the transatlantic arbitrage window is nearly ready to reopen but gains in NWE prices could put this off for a while.

Some traders saw a gap of around $3 a tonne to be filled before the arbitrage can work, but others said an increase in New York gasoline prices of about 0.50 cent a gallon or a decrease in prices in Europe of the same level could restart transatlantic trade.
Gas oil was expected to strengthen slightly with supply looking a little less sloppy than it has done over the last few weeks.
"I think we'll see less material coming out of the Med which hopefully will help prices here," one trader said.
But despite the slightly less negative tone to the market few traders were expecting anything spectacular.
"The heating oil market should start getting slightly busier over the next few weeks as end-users start to stock up but I'm not looking for any amazing surge in activity," one trader said.
Heating oil barges in Rotterdam were trading at around July IPE +25 cents on Friday.

High sulphur barges were mixed, with some traders saying they will be steady at the start of the week with good prospects for strengthening due to increased demand, with several people said to have needs for that period.
Others however said they would be unchanged to slightly weakish with demand decreasing further into summer and with enough product around.
Low sulphur barges were seen a shade firmer with sellers insisting on $96/$97 and with buyers said to have increased their bids by $1 to about $95 after trades at the higher numbers last week.
High sulphur cargoes was seen steady to slightly firmer if crude holds gains made at the end of last week and with little Russian material on offer in the north.
Low sulphur was seen weakish with traders saying about four cargoes were on offer in early July.
